playstyle: TREASURE IS THE ENGINE, DRAGONS ARE THE PAYOFF. A non-creature treasure engine — enchantments, artifacts and lands — because this pod wipes creatures constantly and an engine built on bodies resets to zero. Treasure buys cards (Academy Manufactor's Clues, Baylen-style sinks), buys damage (Reckless Fireweaver turns every artifact entering into damage to each opponent, with no combat step), and buys Dragons at a discount Eminence grants for free from the command zone. The Ur-Dragon is NOT cast as a plan: Eminence works from the command zone, and if treasure pops off, two Treasures cover the U and B pips and he lands as upside. Deliberately NOT Dragon typal — the cost-reducer and tutor package is cut. BUT CREATURES AND COMBAT ARE A REAL MODE: 26 creatures, 15 of them fliers, 15 Dragons. The rule is VALUE ON ENTRY OR ON DEATH, NEVER ON PERSISTENCE — a wipe cannot undo a trigger that already resolved. Scourge of Valkas and Terror of the Peaks ping on every Dragon entering; Lathliss makes a 5/5 token per nontoken Dragon which triggers both again; Gadrak and Pitiless Plunderer pay when creatures die. Big fliers are wanted, they are simply not the thing the deck depends on. THE COMMANDER'S AXIS IS FIVE-COLOUR ACCESS, AND IT IS ONLY WORTH SOMETHING IF SPENT: Treasures tap for any colour, so the deck takes the best treasure card in every colour rather than staying inside a two- or three-colour identity. Measured, that means BLACK — Black Market Connections (treasure, a card and a body every turn off one enchantment), Revel in Riches, Pitiless Plunderer, Crux of Fate, Toxic Deluge, Demonic Tutor. BLUE IS DELIBERATELY UNSPENT: its best cards for this deck are colourless ones needing no splash at all. Eminence still discounts 12 Dragons; the attack trigger is unused upside, not the plan.
notes: Refactor prompted by the 2026-08-25 pod debrief (log 002) and docs/ur-dragon-fork.md. THE FORK DOC'S 132-DEMAND FIGURE WAS A PROPERTY OF THE OLD CARD LIST, NOT OF THE COMMANDER: colour identity is a deckbuilding permission and imposes no mana cost. An RGW-only 99 under The Ur-Dragon demands 80 sources at 1.7 colours per producer, identical to any Naya commander. Off-colour splashes are cast off Treasures and must be SORCERY-SPEED ONE-SHOTS — an instant held up means Treasures kept untapped across every opponent's turn, which is the exact structural failure the debrief found in Edgar. Design rule: prefer cards that do two or more jobs (a body AND a treasure, a treasure AND a card). MANA BASE IS RGW ONLY — no Swamps and no black duals. Black is cast entirely off Treasures plus four fixers, and three of those four are BETTER because the commander is five-colour: Arcane Signet and Commander's Sphere tap for any colour in the commander's identity (WUBRG), Mox Jasper taps for any colour while you control a Dragon (15 of them), and Chromatic Lantern alone turns all 36 lands into black sources. That is ~31 ways to make black with zero black lands. Crux of Fate is the only two-pip off-colour card and is worth it: with 15 Dragons, 'destroy all non-Dragon creatures' is a one-sided wipe.
